root_cause.text: The code allowed userspace to specify a helper via CTA_EXPECT_HELP_NAME that could differ from the master conntrack's helper, leading to validation of CTA_EXPECT_CLASS against the user-specified helper's class range instead of the actual master helper's range, causing a slab-out-of-bounds read when the expectation is used with the master helper.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the lookup and use of a user-provided helper in `ctnetlink_alloc_expect` and `ctnetlink_create_expect`, and now always uses `rcu_dereference(help->helper)` from the master conntrack before validating `CTA_EXPECT_CLASS`. The commit message states this was "uncovered when validating CTA_EXPECT_CLASS via different helper provided by userspace than the existing master conntrack helper", leading to the KASAN slab-out-of-bounds in `nf_ct_expect_related_report`.
